title: On-Call Incident
description: Sparse, triage-first view for a paged engineer: firing alerts, golden signals clipped to the incident window, and Anthropic-specific error breakdown so a rate-limit reads distinctly from a real bug. Not for browsing -- see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-13-sre-dashboard-strategy-design.md. This dashboard does not depend on GA checklist item 3.11 (Alertmanager symptom-based rules) to be useful -- ALERTS already reflects kube-prometheus-stack's default infra alerts; 3.11 adds more rows here once it lands, it doesn't unblock this dashboard's existence.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: ALERTS{alertstate="firing"} -- every currently-firing alert, infra-level (kube-prometheus-stack defaults) or app-level (once GA checklist 3.11 lands), in one place.

panels.title: Error rate, /query + /auth (last 30m)
panels.description: (sum(rate(openlex_http_requests_total{route=~"/query|/auth.*",status_class="5xx"}[5m])) OR on() vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(rate(openlex_http_requests_total{route=~"/query|/auth.*"}[5m])) OR on() vector(0), 1e-9) -- clamp_min on the denominator avoids a 0/0 NaN (dropped by Grafana as a gap) whenever there's no traffic in a given 5m bucket, which is frequent at this traffic volume.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(openlex_http_requests_total{route=~"/query|/auth.*",status_class="5xx"}[5m])) OR on() vector(0)) / clamp_min(sum(rate(openlex_http_requests_total{route=~"/query|/auth.*"}[5m])) OR on() vector(0), 1e-9)

panels.title: Anthropic call outcomes by status (last 30m)
panels.description: sum by (status) (rate(openlex_anthropic_requests_total[5m])) -- rate_limited reads distinctly from api_error and success, so an Anthropic-side throttle is never mistaken for an OpenLex bug mid-incident.

panels.title: Slowest /query traces (last 30m)
panels.description: TraceQL search for the slowest spans in the incident window -- click through to the full waterfall in Tempo.
